methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Carbyon is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Hans De Neve. The valuation framework draws on a comp universe of one public peer (LNZA) and eight private companies in the Climate & Energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. To date, Carbyon has raised €22.3M.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised (€22.3M) as a proxy for current post-money valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to subsequent stage, the analysis implies a valuation of €45M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy peer set; while eight sector peers exist, none met the filtering thresholds necessary for reliable statistical triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €38M to €51M, with a median point of €45M. This range reflects a ±15% band around the stage-progression midpoint. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to later-stage peers, unit economics not captured in raise size, and the limited public comp set for direct valuation benchmarking in this sector. The single applicable method constrains confidence; materiality of revenue, burn rate, or product development stage could materially shift the indicated range.
